title: Measure security boundaries and residual authority
purpose: Help developers and security practitioners explain what controls prevent, detect and still permit in a trading application. Learn in phases before comparing runtime products.
entryAssumptions: C3 normal trading and its Kubernetes runtime are understood; no production data is used.
concepts: A reachable destination is not unlimited database authority; scoped service authority is not end-user business authorization.
An alert or killed process does not prove that impact was prevented.
runtimePrerequisites: The integrated state is planned. Prototype onboarding is explicitly limited to its verified host and fixture scope; run only one full cluster at a time.

transitions.motivation: A working application does not yet explain its security boundaries.
transitions.increment: Add staged controls, bounded experiments and independent outcome evidence.
transitions.evidence: Positive trading plus attributable negative checks and residual-authority outcomes in the same pinned deployment.

after: Target: learners can reproduce and explain layered security and residual risk; integrated acceptance is pending.

objectives.outcome: Explain which security layer intervened using correlated decisions and independent state evidence.
Distinguish denied out-of-grant operations from residual misuse of legitimate service authority, then compare detection with prevention.
Reproduce a bounded experiment, restore synthetic data and verify that legitimate trading continues within a measured resource budget.

walkthrough.action: Planned integrated walkthrough: predict a decision, run positive and negative controls, inspect effects, compare runtime modes and reset. Prototype checkpoint evidence is available separately.
walkthrough.expected: Attribute each decision and resulting state; do not infer prevention from an alert or claim a fixture is integrated.

assessments.question: A service talks to its allowed database and a runtime alert fires. What proves prevention and successful recovery?
assessments.guidance: Inspect independent canary and downstream effects after settling, compare the same inputs across profiles, reset and rerun positive trading; record resource costs and limitations.

limitations: Planned generated state; current evidence covers individual checkpoints and candidate integrations only.
CVE/OSERA is optional and planned; CALM is a separate successor. Local checks are not compliance certification.

coaching.diagnosticQuestion: Which identity and authority does each boundary actually enforce?
coaching.predictionPrompt: Predict whether a within-grant write by a compromised service will be distinguishable from normal work.
hints: Follow the identity from the user through the process and database role.
Inspect final state independently; an alert is a separate observation.
coaching.misconception: Strong networking or a runtime alert guarantees that all business-unauthorized writes are prevented.
coaching.evidenceToRequest: Pinned configuration, correlated decisions, independent before/after outcomes, reset evidence and continued trading.
